fields.meta_title: PayPal Donation Form Builder for Nonprofits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a PayPal donation form that tags each gift to a fund, logs monthly gifts, and keeps donor records in a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a PayPal Donation Form That Records Every Gift
fields.hero_description: Build a PayPal donation form that ties each gift to a fund and saves the PayPal transaction in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: The PayPal pop-up takes the gift. The PayPal donation form around it saves the donor, the fund, and the transaction to your database.
fields.feature_1:
A gift form written from one prompt

Describe the funds you raise for and the amounts to suggest. Emergent builds the form, the donor tables, and a staff screen, then changes any of them each time you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Donors stay on your site to pay

The app connects to your PayPal account and opens the Donate pop-up over your page. PayPal says this keeps donors on your website instead of redirecting them to a PayPal page.
fields.feature_3:
The transaction ID saved on the gift

PayPal returns a transaction ID when a gift completes, and the app saves it on the gift row beside the amount and fund. Matching a PayPal statement line to a donor takes one search.
fields.feature_4:
Monthly gifts with every cycle logged

A monthly gift runs as a PayPal subscription, billed at regular intervals. Each cycle, PayPal posts an event to the app, and the payment joins that donor's history as a new row.
fields.feature_5:
First-time donors reach a person

A donor's first gift sends an email or Slack message to whoever writes welcome notes, with the fund and amount attached. A reminder follows 2 days later if no note is marked sent.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the form wherever your website already runs. The PayPal connection and the donor tables go with it.

fields.usecase_heading: What Happens to a Gift After PayPal Takes It
fields.tab_content_1:
For Weekend Backpacks, $60 given in a pop-up

Cobbleford Community Pantry's form asks for a name and a fund before the amount. Oksana Feldmanis picks the Weekend Backpacks fund and pays $60 in the PayPal pop-up over the pantry's page. Her gift row stores the transaction ID PayPal sends back, and the fund's total on the staff screen now counts her $60.
fields.tab_content_2:
Payment 4 is in, and Ilario has given $100

Ilario Pesce set up a $25 monthly gift to Brindle Hollow Animal Rescue, and it runs as a PayPal subscription. On his fourth billing date, PayPal tells the app the payment went through. The app adds payment 4 as a new row under his name, and his record now shows $100 given since he signed up.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every student link rolls up into the boosters' board

Cindermoor High Robotics Boosters gave each of its 14 students a fundraiser link to send to family. A gift that starts from a link carries that student's name into the PayPal pop-up and onto the gift row. The board ranks all 14 by money raised, and Ambrose Tuck leads with $420 from 9 donors.
fields.tab_content_4:
After the refund, $8,300 stands as the chorale's total

Jory Holloran asked Saltmarsh Chorale to return his $150 gift, and it was refunded from the PayPal business dashboard. PayPal reports the refund to the app, which marks the gift Refunded and emails treasurer Ophelia Dunstable with his name and the amount. The year's total was $8,450 and now reads $8,300.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a PayPal Donation Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a PayPal donation form, connect your PayPal account, and test it with a real $1 gift before launch.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every fund a gift can go to
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for a name, a fund, and an amount
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every fund a donor can choose, in the names donors already use, such as Weekend Backpacks or Fresh Produce. Each fund becomes an option on the form and a running total on the staff screen. Retire a fund by hiding it, so past gifts keep their tag.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the donor's name and the fund before the amount, and leave card and bank details to the PayPal pop-up. Suggest amounts such as $25, $60, and $120 based on your recent gifts, with an open field below them for any other figure.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect the PayPal business account that receives your gifts. Place the Donate pop-up on the same page as the form, so a donor picks a fund and pays without being sent to a donation page on PayPal. Keep that page on the domain donors already know.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the funds and suggested amounts into one prompt, along with the PayPal account. Emergent builds the PayPal donation form, the tables behind it, and a screen that totals each fund. Prompt again in March to add a fund or rename one.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Offer a monthly option that runs as a PayPal subscription. Then decide what a monthly donor's record shows, such as every payment as its own row with the amount given to date on top. The record then reads as a history, one payment at a time.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give every volunteer or student who raises money a personal link to the form. Each gift made through it is saved with their name, and a board ranks everyone by money raised. Leave anyone who asks for privacy off the board.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Give a real $1 gift through the live form, then refund it from the PayPal business dashboard. Check that the gift row holds the fund and the transaction ID, that the refund marks it Refunded, and that the treasurer's email arrives.

faq_plan.q: What is a PayPal donation form?
faq_plan.a: A PayPal donation form is a web form that takes a gift and processes the payment through PayPal. It collects what the organization needs, such as who is giving, to which fund, and how much, then opens PayPal to take the payment. The gift record stays with the organization.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a PayPal donation form?
faq_plan.a: List your funds and suggested amounts, and link the PayPal account where gifts should land. Describe the funds and where each gift should be saved to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt. It builds the form and the gift database, and you change either by prompting again. Run one real gift through it, and refund it, before launch.

faq_plan.q: Can donors pick a fund on a PayPal donation form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the fund on the form before the PayPal pop-up opens, then save that choice on the gift row with the amount. Each fund's total is then a sum over your own gift table, not a report you export and clean up. With Emergent, that table belongs to you, in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a PayPal donation form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short: the donor's name, the fund, and the amount, with suggested amounts above an open field. Card and bank details belong in the PayPal pop-up, which keeps the form short on a phone. Record checks and cash handed over at an event on a general donation form instead.

faq_plan.q: How do monthly gifts work on a PayPal donation form?
faq_plan.a: PayPal treats a monthly gift as a subscription that bills the donor at regular intervals rather than once. Offer it as a choice beside the one-time gift, and make it the default only once your own numbers show donors pick it. Put the date of the next payment on each monthly donor's receipt.

faq_plan.q: Can one PayPal donation form handle several campaigns at once?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent sets no response caps on the forms it builds, and one form can carry every campaign. Add a campaign tag to each link that points at the form. A gift from the spring appeal and one from the gala then land in the same table with different tags, and each campaign gets its own total.

faq_plan.q: Can a PayPal donation form collect payment for auction items?
faq_plan.a: It can, but keep auction payments apart from gifts. Collect bids on a silent auction form, then send each winner a payment request for the winning amount. Save those payments in their own table, apart from the fund totals.

faq_plan.q: How do refunds show up on PayPal donation forms?
faq_plan.a: Through a webhook. PayPal can post an event to your app when a refund is started from the PayPal business dashboard, and the app marks the gift Refunded. Keep the refunded row instead of deleting it. The donor's history and the year's total then both show what changed.

faq_plan.q: Where should a PayPal donation form go on my website?
faq_plan.a: Give it its own page, and link that page from the main menu with one plain label such as Donate. Keep the PayPal pop-up on that page, where donors finish without leaving it. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, ready to host next to the rest of your site.

faq_plan.q: How do fundraiser links work on a PayPal donation form?
faq_plan.a: Each fundraiser gets a personal link to the same form. The link carries their name into the gift. Every gift made through it counts toward their total on a shared board. To recruit more fundraisers, ask current donors for names through a referral form, then send each new volunteer a link.

plan.angle: Searchers for a PayPal donation form find PayPal's own button docs and generic form builders; neither shows what happens to the gift record. This page shows the form around the PayPal Donate pop-up: the donor picks a fund on the organization's own site, the PayPal transaction ID lands on the gift row, monthly gifts run as PayPal subscriptions whose every cycle is logged, student fundraiser links roll up to one board, and a refund started in the PayPal business dashboard comes off the total. Builder intent only; PayPal is the processor the reader already uses, no partnership implied.
